questions.prompt: In Role-Based Access Control, which statement best describes Roles and permissions?
options: Middleware runs in registered order. Each function must end the response, call next() to continue, or forward an error; avoid accidentally doing more than one of these.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Authorization checks what the verified identity may do. Enforce permissions and resource ownership in the server for every protected operation; hiding a button is not access control.
questions.answer_key: Authorization checks what the verified identity may do. Enforce permissions and resource ownership in the server for every protected operation; hiding a button is not access control.
questions.explanation: Authorization checks what the verified identity may do. Enforce permissions and resource ownership in the server for every protected operation; hiding a button is not access control.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Role-Based Access Control?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Authentication answers who is making a request; authorization answers what that identity may do. Hash passwords with established libraries, enforce access on the server, and design sessions/tokens for expiration and revocation.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Authentication answers who is making a request; authorization answers what that identity may do. Hash passwords with established libraries, enforce access on the server, and design sessions/tokens for expiration and revocation.
questions.explanation: Authentication answers who is making a request; authorization answers what that identity may do. Hash passwords with established libraries, enforce access on the server, and design sessions/tokens for expiration and revocation.

questions.prompt: A change related to Role-Based Access Control appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
